about.title: About Compound Interest Calculator
about.description: The Compound Interest Calculator demonstrates the power of compound interest over time. This essential financial tool helps you understand how your investments and savings can grow exponentially when interest is reinvested and earns additional returns. Whether you're planning for retirement, education savings, or long-term wealth building, this calculator shows the dramatic difference compound interest makes compared to simple interest calculations.

howTo.title: How to Use the Compound Interest Calculator

steps.title: Enter Principal Amount
steps.description: Input your initial investment or savings amount that will earn compound interest.

steps.title: Set Interest Rate
steps.description: Enter the annual interest rate (APR) offered by your investment or savings account.

steps.title: Choose Compounding Frequency
steps.description: Select how often interest compounds: daily, monthly, quarterly, or annually.

steps.title: Set Time Period
steps.description: Enter the investment duration in years to see long-term compound growth.

steps.title: Add Regular Contributions
steps.description: Optionally add regular monthly or annual contributions to boost growth.

steps.title: Analyze Results

faq.q: What is compound interest and how does it work?
faq.a: Compound interest is interest calculated on both the initial principal and previously earned interest. It creates exponential growth as your earnings generate their own earnings over time, often called 'interest on interest'.

faq.q: How often should interest be compounded for maximum growth?
faq.a: More frequent compounding (daily vs annually) results in slightly higher returns. However, the difference becomes less significant with higher interest rates and longer time periods. Daily compounding typically provides the best growth.

faq.q: What's the difference between compound and simple interest?
faq.a: Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount. Compound interest is calculated on principal plus accumulated interest, resulting in exponentially higher returns over time. The difference becomes dramatic over long periods.

faq.q: How do regular contributions affect compound growth?
faq.a: Regular contributions significantly boost compound growth by continuously adding new principal that also earns compound interest. Even small regular contributions can have dramatic long-term effects due to the power of compounding.
